purpose: Record every mechanics iteration as an explicit, reproducible before/after hypothesis test. This ledger is process evidence; benchmark outputs and solver qualification diagnostics remain the numerical authority.

measurementPolicy.improvementRule: An iteration is an improvement only when target errors decrease without weakening solver/profile tolerances, changing the reference data, or violating residual/equilibrium/canonical invariants.

baseline.canonicalOrFalsificationEvidence: Incident element-end action sums agree with reported restraint components to the existing benchmark audit tolerance, so the primary mismatch is upstream of reaction reporting.

iterations.hypothesis: Restarting MEC-21 Part II equation (2.25) independently on every numerical bend chord is kinematically subdivision invariant.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: Added a cumulative-station MEC-21 state API and an independent quarter-bend closed-form/falsification fixture; solver behavior was not changed in this iteration.

iterations.hypothesis: Sampling one physical bend-level MEC-21 free field at both ends of every stiffness chord in a single fixed bend-start a-b-c basis correctly represents the cumulative pressure free field while preserving the qualified linear solver and recovery contracts.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: ACCDB adapter sampled cumulative bend stations, mapped literal MEC-21 a-b-c components through one fixed bend-start basis, transformed the resulting two-end generalized displacement with d_local = T d_global, and formed f0 = K_effective d0. No solver, restraint, tolerance, B31/B31J stiffness, or recovery-sign change.

canonicalOrFalsificationEvidence.selfReviewFinding1: The first angular-closure guard snapped the final cumulative angle before measuring the residual, so that guard could not detect a bad chord-angle sum.
canonicalOrFalsificationEvidence.selfReviewFinding2: MEC-21 final-point a-b-c coordinates rotate with bend station angle; a fixed bend-start basis is not the governing transformation when literal equation components are used directly.

iterations.hypothesis: MEC-21 equation (2.25) bend pressure translations are components in the final-station local basis, and transforming that rotating basis to the bend-start basis must match an independent curvature-change integration.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: No solver behavior changed. Performed an independent coordinate/kinematic derivation before revising I002.

canonicalOrFalsificationEvidence.independentDerivation: Integrating the first-order tangent change caused by a uniform curvature reduction over s in [0,R*theta] gives the same bend-start translation components.
canonicalOrFalsificationEvidence.sourceContract: MEC-21 Part II sections 2.3.1, 2.3.5.2 and 2.4 define element flexibility/free movement at the final point in local a-b-c coordinates and the displacement coordinate transformation.

iterations.hypothesis: The station-rotating transformation of MEC-21 equation (2.25) is numerically identical to the independently integrated curvature-change field for any station subdivision, while the fixed bend-start interpretation is not.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: Extended the governed B-3.18 bend check with rotating station axes, independent integrated-curvature translations, a fixed-basis falsification metric, and explicit historical restart labeling. Solver behavior was not changed.

iterations.hypothesis: If the branch-local cumulative-state API resolves MEC-21 final-station components into the physical bend-initial a-b-c basis, the existing BM4 adapter's fixed bend-start mapping becomes the correct cumulative nodal free field without changing solver, stiffness, restraints, or recovery.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: Kept deriveMec21BendPressureFreeMovement as literal STATION_FINAL_ABC Eq. (2.25). Changed deriveMec21BendPressureFreeState to return the same physical state resolved in BEND_INITIAL_ABC and retain the literal final-local components as qualification evidence. Updated the governed bend check to bind both basis contracts. The ACCDB adapter and linear solver code were not changed in this iteration; their behavior changes only through the corrected cumulative-state contract.

iterations.hypothesis: A canonical ACCDB benchmark package can be captured once from the authoritative Windows/ACE extraction and replayed cross-platform without losing source/model identity, so later solver improvements can be measured against exactly the same normalized input.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: Added a package capture/replay command that reuses requiredCaesarAccdbTables, buildCaesarAccdbBenchmarkPackage and solveCaesarAccdbLinearBenchmark; validates model and package semantic hashes; permits machine-local relinking without changing identity; requires --package-out on capture and --actual-out on solves; added a tamper-detection check and an L19-only gate profile.

iterations.hypothesis: The repository already contains a serialized canonical BM4_NL package sufficient to rerun I005 without Windows/ACE extraction.
iterations.codeOrConfigurationDelta: No solver or mechanics change. Searched benchmark and report artifacts for a source-hash-bound package/model table set before attempting to reuse prior output as input.
